text:
maya: heads up — after rolling cilium 1.24 to east2 this morning we're seeing intermittent east-west packet drops for GPU workloads. started ~06:10. pods lose connectivity for ~200-800ms then recover. affecting multi-pod training jobs that use intra-node RDMA fallback.

maya: example: two trainer pods on different nodes, execs show large resend counts and stalled kv-cache syncs. not full node network outage — controlplane & kube-proxy fine.

maya: tcpdump snippet from pod0 -> pod1 (shortened):
```
09:12:34.123456 IP 10.64.5.12.56012 > 10.64.6.45.9090: Flags [P.], seq 1234:2234, ack 3456, win 512
09:12:34.324567 IP 10.64.5.12 > 10.64.6.45: ICMP 10.64.6.45 unreachable - administrative prohibited
09:12:34.900001 IP 10.64.6.45.9090 > 10.64.5.12.56012: Flags [.], seq 3456, ack 2234, win 256, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 654321]
```

maya: also seeing MTU mismatch hints in dmesg on host: kernel reports fragmentation attempts on geneve device.

devin: thanks — can you capture `ip -s link show geneve0` and `ethtool -k <iface>` on both nodes? suspect geneve/gso/gro interaction after cilium's tunnel reassembly change.

maya: grabbing now — pasted below.
```
# ip -s link show geneve0
3: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 12345678 packets 98765 errors 0 dropped 12 overruns 0
    TX: bytes 87654321 packets 123456 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0
# sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
# ethtool -k eth0
features: rx-checksumming: on\nfeatures: tx-checksumming: on\n```

oliver: that MTU 1450 / geneve is telling. our hosts are 9001-enabled but we set cluster MTU to 1450 for tunnel overhead. question: did the 1.24 patch flip tunnel reassembly to `on` by default? that can drop large fragmented UDP packets for RDMA over UDP/encap.

leah: confirmed in canary logs — cilium-agent shows `TunnelReassembly: enabled` after upgrade. we didnt explicitly set it in helm values.

leah: also seeing a pattern where pods scheduled on the same rack node group get stuck and the scheduler retries create extra pods => consumes GPU slots briefly, then they fail backoff. cost spike noticed in the last billing window for east2-gpu because jobs kept restarting. :money_with_wings:

ramon: short mitigation: flip `tunnelReassembly: false` via CiliumConfig and rollout to east2 only, or temporarily bump node MTU to 9000 to avoid fragmentation. prefer config flip first.

devin: agree. rolling MTU is disruptive for other services. config toggle is quicker. we should also capture `ss -s` and `dmesg` around the time window to correlate.

maya: I'm prepping the CiliumConfig patch. will apply to the `east2-gpu` node pool first and watch. patch:
```
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumConfig
metadata:
  name: tunnel-reassembly-toggle
spec:
  tunnelReassembly: false
```

sre-bot: ALERT: net-perf-canary-east2 failed 06:23 -> 06:31. 12% pkt-loss observed in 1m windows (threshold 1%). Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1184.

oliver: nice, thanks @maya. after patch, run `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/cilium` and `kubectl get pods -n gpu -o wide` to see scheduler effects. i'll stand by to revert if it worsens.

maya: applied patch to canary subset (3 nodes). restarting cilium pods now.

maya: quick status: within 5m, the canary jobs show stable connections, no RDMA handshake timeouts in logs. network drops went from 12% -> 0.4% in the canary window.

leah: great. can we run a controlled soak for 2h before org-wide roll? need to ensure nothing else relies on reassembly. also file a follow-up with Cilium upstream, sounds like a breaking default change.

ramon: filing PR to ops-runbooks to add `tunnelReassembly` check to upgrade checklist.

devin: action items: (1) maya to coordinate 2h canary soak on east2-gpu (2) oliver to prepare rollback playbook and MTU bump notes (3) leah to open upstream issue/PR vs cilium 1.24 changelog.

maya: assigned and will post results here. thanks all :pray:
